title: A short thesis does not create a short position
briefing:
Case briefing and follow-up situation

A hypothetical asset is quoted at $100 and your research expects it could fall. You hold zero units. TradeHQ’s supported sell operation disposes of owned spot units; it does not borrow assets or open short positions. Use this case to distinguish a directional idea, a manual sale of a holding and a different product’s leveraged or borrowed exposure.

For a separate spot-account branch, suppose you own three units bought earlier and the quote is still $100. You choose to sell two owned units with the 0.1% fee. Calculate cash received and units remaining. Then let the quote fall to $90 without another order. The unowned-units branch and the owned-sale branch have different valid actions; a bearish thesis alone creates neither borrowed exposure nor an executed sale.

Hypothetical case inputs — not a live market chart · units
Owned units
0
Proposed sell units
2

questions.prompt: Can selling two unowned units open a short on TradeHQ?
options: No; the simulator does not implement short selling
Yes; every sell button borrows units
Yes; a bearish note supplies collateral
questions.feedback:
That’s right.

A bearish idea does not alter the product’s supported mechanics. Selling an owned spot holding and borrowing an asset to sell short are different operations; TradeHQ only implements the former.

questions.prompt: What supported action could reduce existing spot exposure?
options: Manually sell some units already owned
Create a negative holding by journaling
Request borrowed assets from the leaderboard
questions.feedback:
Here’s the reasoning.

Selling owned units reduces the quantity held and returns net proceeds to virtual cash. It does not create a profit from a future fall after the position is closed, nor does it establish a borrowed liability.

questions.prompt: How should an educational short-sale example be labelled?
options: A conceptual worksheet outside supported simulator orders
A guaranteed way to profit from a decline
questions.feedback:
That’s right.

A lesson can explain short mechanics while clearly separating them from the available simulator. Borrowing costs, losses and execution constraints would also matter in a real short; a direction prediction alone is incomplete.

questions.prompt: In the owned-units branch, what is gross notional for selling two units at $100?
questions.feedback:
Here’s the reasoning.

Two owned units multiplied by the $100 quote gives $200 sale notional. The third unit remains held unless a separate valid sell order includes it.

questions.prompt: What fee applies to that $200 spot sale?
questions.feedback:
That’s right.

Multiply $200 by 0.001 to obtain $0.20. The fee is charged on sale notional rather than on the number of units or an assumed future decline.

questions.prompt: What net sale cash is received in the owned-units branch?
questions.feedback:
Here’s the reasoning.

Subtract the $0.20 transaction fee from $200 gross sale value. Net proceeds enter cash and are separate from the mark of any units remaining.

questions.prompt: How many spot units remain after selling two of three owned units?
questions.feedback:
That’s right.

Subtract the two sold units from the three previously owned. The result is one positive spot holding, not a borrowed short position.

questions.prompt: At a subsequent $90 quote, what is the remaining one-unit holding worth?
questions.feedback:
Here’s the reasoning.

One remaining unit times $90 gives $90 marked value. The completed two-unit sale’s cash receipt is not rewritten by this later quote.

questions.prompt: What is the remaining holding’s change from its $100 pre-move mark?
questions.feedback:
That’s right.

Only one unit remains exposed to the $10 quote decline. Reducing spot exposure avoids some further loss but does not create a separate gain from unowned short units.

questions.prompt: Which feature would be required to profit directly from a new borrowed short position?
options: A sell attempt with zero owned units
A product supporting borrowing and short exposure
questions.feedback:
Here’s the reasoning.

Opening borrowed short exposure needs mechanics the simulator does not provide. A directional idea or invalid sale attempt cannot create that financial product.
